facts: The phrase "raining cats and dogs" originated in seventeenth-century England. During heavy rainstorms, many homeless animals would drown and float down the streets, giving the appearance that it had actually rained cats and dogs.
Most experts believe humans domesticated dogs before donkeys, horses, sheep, goats, cattle, cats, or chickens.
The earliest European images of dogs are found in cave paintings dating back 12,000 years ago in Spain.
A dog's sense of smell is so powerful that they can detect a drop of blood in a large swimming pool.
It is a myth that dogs are color blind. They can actually see in color, just not as vividly as humans. It is akin to our vision at dusk.
